one_line: Jain merchant-patron Dharna Shah and architect Deepaka, visionaries behind the 15th‑century Adinath temple at Ranakpur in the Aravalli foothills.

appearance.age_look: Both appear in their early 40s, lean but dignified, with the poised bearing of prosperous professionals used to negotiation and planning.
appearance.face: Both have oval faces with straight noses and medium brown complexions; Dharna’s features are softer with fine lines at the eyes and a calm, compassionate default expression, while Deepaka’s jaw is slightly squarer with a focused, analytical gaze and faint frown of concentration.
appearance.hair: Dharna’s hair is black with a few subtle grey strands, neatly tied into a low nape bun under a simple white Marwari-style turban with a narrow saffron band; Deepaka’s black hair is shorter and combed back, wrapped in a pale indigo cloth turban with a small knot over the left temple and no ornament.
appearance.costume: Dharna wears a long, knee-length off-white cotton angarkha with a side tie and subtle narrow vertical weave, over a plain white dhoti wrapped in the Rajasthani style, pleated in front and reaching the ankles, paired with a light cream shawl with thin maroon borders draped over his left shoulder, simple brown leather mojari shoes, and a single modest gold ring and thin gold chain at the neck; Deepaka wears a slightly shorter pale-cream cotton jama (front-opening, tied with a fabric belt) with faint grey checks, over a soft indigo-dyed cotton churidar that gathers at the ankles, a darker indigo patka (waist sash) knotted at his left hip, sturdy dark brown leather sandals, and a simple palm-leaf measuring cord looped at his waist, both men fully clothed and modest in era-accurate Maru-Gurjara-influenced attire appropriate to 15th-century western India.
appearance.signature: A single detailed rolled architectural plan and measuring set—Dharna holds a rolled palm-leaf manuscript secured with a red thread, while Deepaka carries a wooden measuring rod and a small brass compass tied together with cord, usually held in his left hand.

ref_desc: Dharna Shah and architect Deepaka are two early‑40s, medium‑brown men with oval faces, black hair in simple turbans, wearing off‑white and indigo Maru‑Gurjara‑era angarkha and jama outfits with dhoti and churidar, holding a rolled palm‑leaf architectural plan, wooden measuring rod and brass compass in off‑white, cream, indigo, saffron and brown tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two distinct but coordinated male characters from 15th-century western India standing side by side in front of faint, non-distracting hints of temple pillars: first, Dharna Shah, early 40s, medium brown complexion, oval face with soft features and a calm, compassionate default expression, straight nose and fine smile lines at the eyes, black hair with a few grey strands tied into a low nape bun under a simple white Marwari-style turban with a narrow saffron band; he wears a long, knee-length off-white cotton angarkha with a side tie and subtle narrow vertical weave, over a plain white dhoti wrapped Rajasthani style with front pleats down to the ankles, a light cream shawl with thin maroon borders draped over his left shoulder, simple brown leather mojari shoes, a thin gold neck chain and single modest gold ring, fully clothed and modest, holding a rolled palm-leaf manuscript tied with red thread in his right hand; second, architect Deepaka, also early 40s with a slightly squarer jaw and focused, analytical gaze, medium brown complexion and straight nose, default expression serious but composed, black hair shorter and combed back, wrapped in a pale indigo cloth turban with a small knot over the left temple; he wears a slightly shorter pale-cream cotton jama that opens at the front and ties with a fabric belt, decorated only with faint grey checks, over a soft indigo cotton churidar gathered at the ankles, a darker indigo patka (waist sash) knotted on his left hip, sturdy dark brown leather sandals, and a simple palm-leaf measuring cord looped at his waist, fully clothed and modest, carrying in his left hand a wooden measuring rod and a small brass compass tied together with cord; show both characters in consistent off-white, cream, indigo, saffron and brown tones, with clear front views emphasizing their faces, turbans, garments, footwear and the shared signature architectural tools so they can be redrawn identically in many panels.
